A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a stereo matching benchmark for human face reconstruction, and we have shown that the most efficient stereo algorithms are not necessarily the most accurate for this application.
, for the human face reconstruction problem, the most efficient algorithm is the graph-cut, but it is not the most accurate.
the stereo matching algorithms can be used in the case of human face reconstruction, but the accuracy of the reconstruction is limited by the accuracy of the ground truth model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stereo algorithms are not as good for the human face reconstruction as they are for the reconstruction of general scenes, and that the most efficient algorithm for the general scene reconstruction may not be the most efficient for the human face.
the stereo matching problem is not solved yet, and that more research is needed to improve the accuracy of the algorithms.
there is no single best algorithm for 3D face reconstruction from stereo pairs, and it is up to the user to select the most appropriate algorithm for a particular application.
